title: Regional graceful degradation: session-aware multiplexing and lightweight shadow proxies
creator: Zoe Nakamura
description: Investigate and implement a lightweight regional degradation layer that preserves SLOs during downstream overloads. The solution combines session-aware request multiplexing, tenant-fair admission, and a small per-region shadow proxy that can produce compact soft-responses when Redis/Kafka/primary DB paths are overloaded or experiencing high tail latency. Goal: keep 99th percentile user-facing latency within SLO while avoiding cascading failures and preserving essential correctness for user flows.
acceptance_criteria: Degradation layer is deployable as a per-region sidecar/edge pod with feature flag rollout
99th percentile P95 token/response latency increases by <20% under a simulated downstream outage compared to baseline degraded path
Error rate (5xx) does not exceed current SLO budget for production traffic during controlled failovers
Graceful fallbacks provide documented stub schemas for top 5+ critical endpoints with acceptable UX trade-offs
Automated canary covers one customer with dedicated traffic slice and is reversible within 5 minutes
steps: Design proposal: session-aware multiplexing algorithm and admission controls (complete) - link in linked_docs
Prototype shadow proxy that returns compact soft-responses and partial KV answers from local cache
Integrate token-bucket and per-tenant priority lanes into the proxy for fair shedding
Run chaos test in staging: throttle Redis and increase Kafka lag; collect SLO metrics and dashboards
Iterate on response schemas for UX teams and product stakeholders
Roll out to us-east region behind feature flag, monitor for 48 hours, then promote to eu-west
Postmortem template and runbook drafted for incidents triggered by proxy behavior
notes: Trade-offs considered: returning soft-responses preserves overall availability but risks subtle data consistency/user confusion for read-after-write flows
We chose session-aware multiplexing to reduce burst amplification from hot sessions—this avoids creating new connection pools per session while still honoring affinity
Shadow proxy intentionally keeps logic minimal (no new persistent store); uses local KV cache + deterministic stub templates to simplify rollbacks
Instrumentation is critical: we will tag all degraded responses with header X-RW-Degraded: true and include degrade_reason code for analytics
Latency target is strict because several higher-level flows are latency-sensitive (Console query previews and API synchronous responses)
